papers.title: A Dual Soft Attention Network for Automatic Sleep Staging via Single-Lead Electrocardiogram Signals.
papers.abstract: Polysomnography (PSG) is the current gold standard for sleep monitoring; however, it is complex, burdensome, and costly. In contrast, commercial health monitoring devices, such as the Apple Watch, offer sleep scoring at a low cost over a few days. This paper proposes a dual-attention mechanism-based sleep staging method using single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) signals, named SleepECGNet. The method extracts multi-scale features by employing convolutional kernels of different sizes, thereby capturing subtle details in the ECG signals. The model then integrates an SE module and a Luong attention-based encoder-decoder architecture to filter redundant information and dynamically focus on different sleep stages. Experiments were conducted using the HMC, MGH, and SHHS1 datasets for sleep staging tasks and the Apnea-ECG corpus was employed to execute transfer learning strategies directed at sleep apnea recognition. Comprehensive ablation experiments were conducted to verify the effectiveness of each component. Moreover, an analysis of sequence duration demonstrated that expanding the input timeframe directly improves classification outcomes.

papers.title: Language-supervised electrocardiogram interpretation with vision transformer.
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: Most artificial intelligence models for electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation rely on task-specific supervised learning, requiring dedicated labeled datasets for each diagnostic task and limiting scalability across diverse cardiac conditions. This study investigated whether vision-language learning from paired ECG recordings and summary reports could enable transferable ECG representations without task-specific supervised training.

METHODS: We developed ECG-VLM, a contrastive vision-language model consisting of a Transformer-based image encoder and a text encoder, trained on 800,034 paired 10-s ECG recordings and summary reports from the MIMIC-IV-ECG database. Cardiac condition detection was performed using natural-language prompts without condition-specific retraining or fine-tuning. Performance was evaluated on an internal test set and externally validated using the LSAS-ECG dataset (45,151 recordings) across 14 cardiac conditions, together with retrieval and subgroup analysis.

RESULTS: ECG-VLM achieved diagnostic performance across 14 cardiac conditions, with AUROC ranging from 0.679 to 0.981 on the internal test set and from 0.691 to 0.991 on external validation. Performance was strongest for rhythm abnormalities (mean AUROC 0.948 internally and 0.921 externally) and lower for morphological conditions. Compared with the previously reported signal-based ECG-CLIP framework, ECG-VLM achieved comparable performance for rhythm abnormalities while improving AUPRC for several morphological conditions. Performance remained broadly consistent across external validation and demographic and clinical subgroups.

CONCLUSION: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of vision-language supervision from paired ECG recordings and summary reports for learning transferable ECG representations without task-specific supervised training. This framework provides a basis for future extension of vision-language learning to ECG images encountered in routine clinical practice.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13755-026-00482-7.

papers.title: Memristor-based echo state network for ECG classification: optimizing accuracy and efficiency with different architectures.
papers.abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) signal classification is a crucial task in automated cardiac monitoring and early disease detection. Conventional machine learning and deep learning methods often face challenges related to high computational costs, large data requirements and difficulty in handling real-time ECG analysis. In this work, we have proposed three memristor-based echo state network (MESN) models for ECG classification: (1) MESN, (2) Parallel MESNs (PMESN) with a classifier and (3) Attention-enhanced MESN (AMESN), where all three models employ artificial neural network (ANN) as a readout layer. These models leverage the property of an ESN to transform ECG signals into high-dimensional representations, thereby enhancing classification performance. The proposed models were evaluated on different benchmark ECG datasets: ECG200, ECG5000, ECGFiveDays, NonInvasiveFetalECGThorax1, NonInvasiveFetalECGThorax2, and TwoLeadECG. The results demonstrate that AMESN achieves the highest precision, recall, F1-score and overall accuracy particularly excelling in datasets with high intra-class variability. Whereas, PMESN improves robustness by leveraging multiple reservoir layers, while MESN provides a strong baseline with computational efficiency. These models are also compared with other state-of-the-art models and the analysis shows that AMESN achieves 1.92-13.39% higher accuracy, demonstrating superior performance. These findings highlight the potential of ESN as a lightweight yet powerful approach for ECG classification, making it suitable for integration into wearable and IoT-based healthcare systems.

papers.title: AI-based multimodal analysis of ECG and clinical data for evaluation for competitive sports participation: The VALETUDO trial.
papers.abstract:
AIMS: Pre-participation cardiovascular screening (PPS) is essential for preventing SCD in athletes, yet ECG interpretation requires expertise and remains resource-intensive. We aimed to evaluate the feasibility and diagnostic performance of a deep learning (DL) model for analysis of clinical data and resting 12‑lead ECG obtained during routine PPS in competitive athletes.

METHODS: In this prospective single center observational study, competitive athletes aged 18 to 60 years and undergoing routine PPS were enrolled. PPS included medical history, physical examination, resting and exercise ECG. Athletes were classified as fit or not fit for competitive sports according to clinical evaluation. Resting ECG and clinical variables were analyzed using a multimodal DL architecture. Model performance was assessed using stratified 10-fold cross-validation against PPS clinical classification.

RESULTS: A total of 526 athletes were enrolled (72% male, median age of 27 years (IQR: 20-41); 166 (32%) had a negative PPS result. The test setting (10-fold cross-validation), the model achieved moderate discrimination with an accuracy of 0.64 ± 0.08, SE 0.68 ± 0.15, SP 0.61 ± 0.17, F1-score 0.72 ± 0.1, PPV 0.80 ± 0.07, NPV 0.48 ± 0.12, AUC 0.72(0.66-0.78). Training performances reached accuracy of 0.70 ± 0.06, SE 0.73 ± 0.12, SP 0.67 ± 0.14, F1-score 0.77 ± 0.07, AUC 0.79 (0.74-0.83).

CONCLUSION: Automated DL-based analysis of 12‑lead ECG during PPS is feasible and showed encouraging diagnostic performance in competitive athletes. Although wider experience and external validation is required, AI-assisted multimodal ECG interpretation may represent a useful adjunct to physician assessment for cardiovascular risk stratification in sport screening programs.

papers.title: IoT-based ECG arrhythmia detection and classification model using an optimization based hybrid deep capsule stacked autoencoder.
papers.abstract: Heart disease is one of the most dangerous diseases, and it is getting worse in adults over the age of 40. Cardiac arrhythmia is defined as an irregular heartbeat, and quick diagnosis and treatment are critical for saving the lives of a huge population. Currently, the arrhythmia classification involves diverse challenges that limit the existing methodologies from attaining the desired results. Some of the major challenges involve signal quality issues, including noise and motion artefacts, class imbalance and dataset limitations, generalization issues due to context variability across patients, real-world deployment and clinical trust. Several methodologies have been introduced to date to focus on these critical issues, but most of them are unable to cover and address the issues altogether. This study offers a novel deep learning-based method for identifying and classifying arrhythmias as a remedy. First, the pre-processing step receives the input data, which includes body temperature, heart rate, blood oxygen level, and ECG signal. Pre-processing is done with min-max normalization and an enhanced wavelet Wiener filtering technique (UP_WWF) in this case. After pre-processing, the input is submitted to the feature extraction stage, which extracts significant features. Features are extracted using an adaptive dense convolutional osprey network where the osprey optimization algorithm is used to tune the parameters of the network for better feature discrimination. Finally, with the help of the extracted features, the various arrhythmia classes are classified using an attention-based deep capsule stacked autoencoder (Att_DCSAE). The proposed framework is evaluated using the MIT-BIH dataset for benchmarking, whereas the constructed combined ECG dataset includes ECG, heart rate, blood oxygen level, and body temperature measurements. The proposed approach resulted in an overall accuracy of 99.6% on the combined ECG dataset, signifying that it can be applied in hard real-world conditions. The study also shows significant improvements when evaluated on the MIT-BIH dataset with a total precision, recall, and F1-score values of 99.98%, 99.68% and 99.86%, resulting in the overall improvement of 0.6% precision, 0.08% recall, and 0.7% F1-score when compared with the latest techniques in the literature.

papers.title: Deep learning analysis of sinus-rhythm echocardiography for the identification of patients with atrial fibrillation.
papers.abstract:
AIMS: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation (AF) is underdiagnosed due to its intermittent and asymptomatic nature. We evaluated whether a deep neural network (DNN) applied to transthoracic echocardiograms (TTEs) acquired in sinus rhythm can discriminate between patients with and without documented AF and identify individuals at increased risk for subsequent AF documentation and adverse outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively analysed 85 686 TTE studies (2009-21). A DNN was applied to apical four-chamber and parasternal long-axis videos without Doppler. AF ground truth was based on International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes, electrocardiogram, Holter, or prior echocardiographic documentation of AF. The dataset was split into training (60%), validation (20%), and an independent test set (20%). In the test cohort, we assessed discrimination performance. Among patients without prior AF, we evaluated associations between model classification and subsequent AF documentation and a composite outcome of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or stroke. The test set included 17 121 patients (median age 66 years [interquartile range, IQR 54-75]; 57.6% male), of whom 3449 (20.1%) had prior AF. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.85, with sensitivity 0.80 and specificity 0.72. At the selected threshold, 6581 patients (38.4%) were classified as model-positive, including 3832 (58.2%) without prior AF. Among patients without prior AF, model-positive classification was associated with subsequent AF documentation [adjusted hazard ratio (HR) 1.64; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.33-2.04] and with the composite outcome (adjusted HR 1.24; 95% CI 1.13-1.35).

CONCLUSION: Deep learning applied to sinus-rhythm TTE demonstrates discrimination for AF and identifies an imaging-derived signal associated with subsequent AF documentation and adverse outcomes.

papers.title: ReBAN-Net: An interpretable hybrid deep learning framework for ECG-based emotion recognition.
papers.abstract: Emotional assessment is essential for mental health management, yet questionnaire-based scales are subjective and facial- or voice-based approaches can be influenced by intentional behavior and environmental interference. This study proposes ReBAN-Net, a hybrid architecture integrating a one-dimensional residual convolutional network, a bidirectional long short-term memory network, and a soft attention mechanism for ECG-based emotion recognition. Three classification tasks were defined throughout the study: nine-class valence classification (levels 1-9), nine-class arousal classification (levels 1-9), and four-class affective-state classification (baseline, stress, amusement, and meditation). The model was evaluated on the WESAD dataset using a strict 15-fold leave-one-subject-out protocol. It achieved accuracies of 86.03% for nine-class valence, 86.27% for nine-class arousal, and 87.58% for four-class affective-state classification, with corresponding macro-AUC values of 96.07%, 96.24%, and 95.09%. Temporal class activation and attention-feature analyses show that the model focuses on physiologically meaningful ECG regions. These results demonstrate the feasibility and interpretability of ReBAN-Net and indicate its potential for subject-independent ECG-based emotion recognition.

papers.title: A clinical decision support system for ECG diagnosis: Surpassing commercial standards through dual-stream feature fusion.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Automated electrocardiogram (ECG) interpretation is essential for clinical efficiency, yet many existing deep learning (DL) models are perceived as "black boxes" and lack direct benchmarking against established commercial standards. To foster clinician trust and support reimbursement justification, AI systems must demonstrate not only superior accuracy but also alignment with established clinical criteria.

METHODS: We proposed a Dual-Stream Signal Fusion Architecture that integrates latent spatio-temporal features from 21,799 raw 12-lead ECG waveforms (PTB-XL) with 148 expert-engineered clinical metrics extracted via commercial algorithms (PTB-XL+). The system was evaluated against the Marquette 12SL™ (12SL) commercial standard using the independent PTB-XL test set (Fold 10).

RESULTS: The proposed Hybrid Model achieved a Macro F1-Score of 0.851, significantly outperforming the commercial 12SL standard (0.812) and the waveform-only baseline (0.821). Notably, sensitivity for Myocardial Infarction (MI) improved by 10.8% relative to 12SL (0.72 vs. 0.65). Feature importance analysis confirmed that the model's decisions are clinically traceable, attributing 45% importance to QRS amplitude for Hypertrophy diagnosis, which aligns with Sokolow-Lyon criteria.

CONCLUSIONS: Our hybrid framework offers a superior, transparent, and robust standard for automated ECG interpretation. By outperforming clinical gold standards and providing physiologically sound reasoning, this work represents a step toward building the clinical evidence base for AI-based diagnostic support across diverse global populations; prospective, multi-site validation remains necessary before clinical deployment can be considered. The proposed framework is further distinguished by its modular design, which ensures adaptability across both resource-rich and resource-limited clinical environments.

papers.title: A novel method for analysis of transient morphological changes in quasiperiodic physiological signals and their neurogenic correlates.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Transient changes in electrocardiographic (ECG) morphology often accompany fluctuations in heart rhythm and may provide clinically relevant information about cardiac function. However, conventional ECG visualization and analysis methods typically emphasize either waveform morphology or rhythm variability, making it difficult to assess their temporal interplay in long-term recordings and, consequently, to identify rhythm-related morphological changes and exploit their potential diagnostic value. This work presents a visualization framework for quasiperiodic physiological signals that enables simultaneous assessment of beat-to-beat morphological changes and rhythm dynamics in a single representation.

METHODS: The proposed method converts quasiperiodic signals into two-dimensional carpet plots. Characteristic events (e.g., ECG R peaks) are used to align consecutive signal segments, which are transformed into color-coded rows and stacked in chronological order. The resulting image preserves both the temporal evolution of signal morphology and variations in cycle duration. The method was evaluated using ECG recordings from multiple publicly available databases containing healthy subjects and patients with diverse cardiac abnormalities, as well as synchronized multimodal physiological recordings.

RESULTS: Carpet plots enabled rapid visualization of transient morphological changes alongside heart rate dynamics across recordings ranging from several minutes to hours. The representation highlighted clinically relevant phenomena, including ST segment alterations, QT interval variability, changes in T wave morphology, atrial fibrillation episodes, premature ventricular complexes, Wenckebach periodicity, and stress-test phase transitions. The image-based representation was also shown to be suitable for automated analysis using convolutional neural network feature extraction.

CONCLUSIONS: Carpet plots provide a compact representation of quasiperiodic physiological signals, jointly visualizing rhythm and morphology across long-term recordings. The proposed framework facilitates both expert interpretation and image-based computational analysis, offering a general approach for investigating transient physiological phenomena in ECG and other synchronized quasiperiodic signals.

papers.title: Per-class conformal risk control for multi-label ECG classification: achieving clinically-justified false negative rate guarantees.
papers.abstract: Objective. Automated electrocardiogram (ECG) classifiers require uncertainty procedures that address class-specific clinical risk in intrinsically multi-label data.Approach. We propose per-class risk-controlling prediction sets for multi-label ECG classification. For each diagnostic class, binary false-negative-rate (FNR) loss is calibrated with a one-sided exact-binomial upper confidence bound. The nine disease-specific targets are controlled simultaneously at 95% family-wise confidence using Bonferroni allocation. The final operating threshold is the more inclusive of the exact-binomial threshold and a conservative reference threshold derived from a concentration bound; this safeguard uses calibration data only and cannot weaken the exact guarantee.Main results. We evaluated the method on PTB-XL (21 388 retained recordings) and Chapman-Shaoxing (10 199 retained recordings), using a patient-disjoint PTB-XL split and fitting-partition-only normalisation. The proposed method met all 9/9 prespecified disease-specific FNR targets on held-out test sets and produced non-vacuous simultaneous exact-binomial guarantees for all nine targets; uniform standard conformal prediction met 5/9. Test FNR was 0.0% for myocardial infarction (exact 95% upper bound 0.35%, at 80.3% FPR), 1.0% for ST/T changes, and 0.3% for atrial fibrillation; the high-sensitivity operating point is purchased with substantially reduced specificity. Under PTB-XL-to-Chapman shift, macro class coverage fell from 94.3% to 45.5%, demonstrating that the guarantees do not transport without local recalibration.Significance. Exact-binomial per-class risk control provides a transparent high-sensitivity operating point for ECG triage while making its specificity, prediction-set-size, calibration-support, and exchangeability limitations explicit.

papers.title: Deep Learning and Dual-Domain Fusion of Temporal and Spectrotemporal SCG for Valvular Heart Disease Classification.
papers.abstract: Heart valve disease (HVD) is a growing cause of cardiovascular morbidity, yet accessible screening tools remain limited. Tri-axial seismocardiogram (SCG) signals capture mechanical signatures of both stenosis and regurgitation, but their non-stationary nature and subtle inter-lesion morphological differences challenge robust classification from a single representation. This study proposes an electrocardiogram (ECG)-free dual-domain deep learning framework that combines a 1D convolutional-recurrent encoder of raw SCG waveforms with a 2D EfficientNet encoder of continuous wavelet transform scalograms, integrating temporal and spectrotemporal representations through feature-level fusion. The framework was evaluated on primary valve lesion classification in 94 patients, with an additional exploratory analysis of multi-valvular, aortic-stenosis-dominant disease. Under patient-level stratified group cross-validation, the fused model achieved the highest mean accuracy (65.3%; 95% CI, 59.8-70.7%), exceeding both unimodal encoders and the majority-class (35.2%) and covariate-only (39.1%) baselines. The same mean performance ordering was preserved when the image backbone was replaced, although the confidence intervals overlap at this cohort size. Under the segment-level protocol used in prior studies, the framework achieved 99.63% accuracy, with faster training convergence and more compact, separable feature clusters than either unimodal encoder. These findings support the value of combining temporal and spectrotemporal SCG representations and demonstrate its potential for ECG-free HVD classification under patient-independent evaluation.

papers.title: Subject-independent framework for protocol-defined stress task classification using multimodal physiological signals.
papers.abstract: Prolonged stress can cause cardiovascular disease, depression, and anxiety. Reliable detection is therefore important. Existing studies using multimodal physiological methods have already reported accuracy, up to 99.7% however, two important aspects remain underexplored. First, most studies separate stress only from a neutral baseline, amusement, and different workload levels. Second, subject-independent performance remains limited because most studies evaluate their models using subject-dependent data splits that are prone to data leakage. This proposed study tries to address these gaps. Protocol-defined stress tasks are detected from everyday activities, not from any workload levels. The proposed model, a one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN), is evaluated subject independently using leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) cross-validation. This proposed study was conducted on the GalaxyPPG dataset. The dataset includes ECG, PPG, and BVP signals. This enables multimodal fusion for stress detection during everyday activities. Single modalities achieve mean test accuracies of 62.19% for PPG, 67.74% for BVP, and 47.81% for ECG on LOSO. Fusion (ECG+PPG+BVP) achieves the mean test accuracy on LOSO evaluation, 76.47% }14.60%. To the best of the author's knowledge, this modality's combination (ECG+PPG+BVP) has not been explored in the literature for GalaxyPPG dataset.

papers.title: Deep learning models to detect neurodegenerative diseases across different modalities, datasets, and stages: A systematic review.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.abstract: BackgroundNeurodegenerative diseases like Alzheimer's and Parkinson's pose significant diagnostic challenges because they are incurable. Their symptoms often overlap with those of normal ageing and involve progressive neuronal loss. This makes early prediction, proper diagnosis, and ongoing monitoring crucial at every stage of the disease. Deep learning has become a useful tool for handling different types of data. However, the performance of these models relies heavily on the availability and variety of data, making it important to characterize datasets.ObjectiveThis PRISMA-based systematic review looks at 111 studies from 2019 to April 2026, organized into three clinical stages of neurodegenerative diseases: early prediction, diagnosis, and progression.MethodsEach study is assessed across four dimensions: data type (neuroimaging or non-neuroimaging), datasets (open-access, self-created, or hybrid), deep learning model architecture, and the use of explainable AI.ResultsMRI is the only imaging modality that spans all three stages. Speech is the most common non-neuroimaging method for diagnosis, while gait is used only for diagnosis and progression. The ADNI and PPMI datasets are the most commonly used. Self-created datasets introduce new modalities such as ECG and iPSCs, which are not found in open-access datasets. CNNs are the leading models for neuroimaging tasks, while LSTMs and RNNs capture temporal patterns in longitudinal datasets. Survival models are exclusively used for ALS and LATE. Fewer than 6% of the studies used confirmed XAI. Only 2 of the 111 studies validated their results on an independent external cohort.ConclusionThis review is the only one that covers all three disease stages across multiple neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Patient and database shift in lightweight ECG arrhythmia classification: a controlled evaluation of noise, quantization, and embedded inference.
papers.abstract: Efficient microcontroller execution does not ensure reliable electrocardiogram classification across patients and databases. We conducted a controlled benchmark of three convolutional architectures under a corrected subject-disjoint MIT-BIH split, external INCART testing, noise stress test database artifacts, 16-bit floating-point (FP16) and full-integer 8-bit (INT8) conversion, and classifier-only invocation on an ESP32 without external RAM. Five fixed seeds were used. On the MIT-BIH test cohort (DS2), INT8 four-class macro-F1 was 0.474-0.498 and supraventricular (S) recall was 0.150-0.180. Mean S-class area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was below 0.5 in all six architecture-regime groups, although all corresponding record-cluster intervals included 0.5. Within-record ranking could remain high despite poor pooled ranking. On INCART, S-class ranking was stronger, with all six patient-cluster AUROC intervals above 0.5, but the representative mixed-noise depthwise-separable convolutional neural network (DS-CNN) achieved 0.797 recall with 0.074 precision. Including record 201, which shares a subject with test record 202, increased DS2 S-recall point estimates by 2.49-14.68 percentage points. In the primary architecture panel, FP16 and INT8 met the engineering tolerances in all 120 comparisons. DS-CNN required 9.49 ms per classifier invocation on the ESP32 using preprocessed, annotation-centered inputs. Acquisition, QRS detection, preprocessing, current, and energy were not measured. Patient-dependentS-score behavior and external false-positive predictions limited this panel more than numerical precision or microcontroller resources.

papers.title: Diagnostic accuracy of artificial intelligence (AI)-based models for acute myocardial infarction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract:
AIMS: Despite continuous improvements in diagnostic tools, the diagnosis of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is still based on electrocardiogram (ECG) and cardiac biomarkers supported by other non-invasive imaging techniques. However, ECG has limited sensitivity, while high-sensitivity troponin assays may show reduced specificity, particularly in older or multimorbid patients. Widely adopted clinical pathways (e.g. ESC 0/1 h algorithm) have reported high diagnostic discrimination in external cohorts (with AUC ranging from 0.93 to 0.96) which provides clinical context for interpreting our findings. These diagnostic tests have limitations that can be addressed through automated computer-based diagnostic systems using Artificial Intelligence (AI). Several studies in the literature have presented machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) models to quickly and accurately assess the diagnosis of AMI to optimize treatment.

METHODS AND RESULTS: The aim of our analysis was to evaluate the performance of AI-based models for the diagnosis of AMI using data from all validation and test cohorts available in literature. Sensitivity and specificity for all MIs, and for STEMI and NSTEMI separately, were analysed for different types of AI approach (non-DL or DL) and for different data sources (ECG or troponin-based). Hierarchical models were used to estimate the summary receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity and specificity.A total of 24 studies evaluating 27 AI-based diagnostic algorithms were included encompassing 166.052 patients, of which 18.850 (11.3%) had a final diagnosis of AMI. Patients were predominantly male (61.8%) with a median age of 60.7 (IQR 59.0-64.1) years. Discrimination of AI-based algorithms for the diagnosis of AMI was high with an AUC of 0.97 (sensitivity 0.93, specificity 0.92). This result remained consistent when considering the ability to diagnose STEMI (AUC 0.96, sensitivity 0.91, specificity 0.94) or NSTEMI (AUC 0.97, sensitivity 0.95, specificity 0.90) separately. No significant difference was found regarding type of AI. ECG and troponin-based models were both extremely accurate, with the first ones being less sensitive and the latter less specific.

CONCLUSIONS: AI-based diagnostic algorithms for AMI diagnosis were associated with particularly efficient performance. These results were consistent for both STEMI and NSTEMI considered separately. Rather than replacing conventional diagnostic pathways, AI has the potential to enhance existing tools by identifying subtle ECG features and integrating multiple data streams. While direct head-to-head comparisons with traditional statistical models are currently limited, future prospective studies evaluating AI and conventional approaches within the same clinical populations are warranted.AI did not lose accuracy depending on the data source or the type of AI applied.
